content_html:
Physics of Information

Information has physical costs and limits. Landauer showed erasing a bit dissipates heat; Bekenstein bound and black‑hole thermodynamics tie information to area. Here we connect these principles to memory as constraint and capacity.

Information is physical. Memory systems obey thermodynamic costs (erasure heat) and capacity limits (entropy bounds). In this view, remembering is the maintenance of low‑entropy distinctions against environmental noise.

Shannon Information: Quantifies uncertainty in messages; connects to compressibility and code length.
Landauer’s Principle: Erasing one bit at temperature T dissipates at least kT ln 2 of heat.
Bekenstein–Hawking Entropy: Maximum information scales with surface area (not volume); black holes encode information on horizons.
